Cache-Control.description: The one-time response must not be stored by HTTP caches.

ETag.description: Opaque strong validator for this representation. Keep its quotation marks and use it as If-Match on a documented conditional write. A replay carries the original ETag, which may now be stale.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: True when the original successful result was replayed for this key.

Location.description: URL of the import to poll.

RateLimit.description: State of the rate-limit policy currently closest to rejection (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): the quoted policy name with `r` = requests remaining right now and `t` = seconds until the full quota is available again. Example: `"api-key";r=42;t=7`. Advisory: absent when the request fails authentication, is rejected before it (a body over the size limit) or the limiter state is momentarily unknown.

RateLimit-Policy.description: The rate-limit policies applied to the request: each quoted policy name with `q` = sustained request quota per window of `w` seconds. Example: `"api-key";q=180;w=60, "workspace";q=600;w=60`. Advisory: absent when the request fails authentication, is rejected before it (a body over the size limit) or the limiter state is momentarily unknown.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: an unknown or invalid query parameter, an invalid id in the path, or a body that is not valid JSON. `code` names the problem, `errors` the parameter or field.

ContentTooLarge.description: The request exceeds the body or upload limit; no operation was performed.

InternalServerError.description: An unexpected internal server error occurred.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or the API key cannot see it.

PreconditionFailed.description: The current representation does not match If-Match (`precondition_failed`). No change was applied.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

TooManyRequests.description: The API rate limit was exceeded. Wait for the number of seconds given in the Retry-After header, then retry.

UnprocessableContent.description: The request is well-formed, but values are invalid; `errors` points at each of them.

AutomationAction.description: What the rule does and to which texts. `type` selects the shape; it follows from the rule's `type` for now.

AutomationAddLabelAction.description: Adds a label to the segment.

label_id.description: The label to add; null when the label no longer exists in the workspace.

type.description: Selects this shape of the body.

AutomationCondition.description: A plain-text condition; conditions in one list must all match.

mode.description: Plain-text matching mode. Regular expressions are not used.

value.description: Match text; null for conditions that require no text value.

AutomationConditionSubject.description: What a condition looks at. `KEY`: the segment's keys; the condition matches when one of them does. `TEXT`: the content of the text. `DESCRIPTION`: the segment's description.

AutomationMatchMode.description: How a condition compares, case-sensitively and as plain text (no regular expressions). `IS_EMPTY` and `IS_NOT_EMPTY` take no `value`. `EQUALS`, `STARTS_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH` and `CONTAINS` compare with `value`, which they require.

AutomationOrigin.description: Where the change comes from. `IMPORT`: an import of files, including Git and integration syncs. `EDITOR`: a key or text changed directly, in the editor or through the API. `ANY`: either. Changes made by LINA or pre-translation don't run automation rules.

AutomationReplaceTextAction.description: Replaces every occurrence of `search` in the text with `replace`.

is_placeholder_excluded.description: Whether placeholders in the text are left unchanged.

replace.description: The replacement; an empty string deletes the found text.

search.description: The plain text to search for, case-sensitively.

type.description: Selects this shape of the body.

AutomationRole.description: Which texts of a segment can start the rule. `SOURCE`: the source text. `TARGET`: a text in a target language. `ANY`: either. A rule that reacts to keys takes `ANY`, because a key has no language.

AutomationScope.description: Which incoming changes may trigger a configured rule.

language_codes.description: Empty means every language; meaningful only for text-level triggers.

items.description: Language code that uniquely identifies a locale. Valid examples would be 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'de-DE' etc. according to [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

origin.description: IMPORT, EDITOR, or ANY. LINA/pretranslation bypass this workflow pipeline.

role.description: Source/target scope; meaningful only for text-level triggers.

AutomationSetStatusAction.description: Sets the status of the texts.

status.description: The status to set.

type.description: Selects this shape of the body.

AutomationTarget.description: Which texts an action writes; separate from trigger scope.

conditions.description: Conditions checked per acted-on target text, separately from trigger conditions.

language_codes.description: Empty means every target language; relevant for SEGMENT_TARGET_TEXTS.

items.description: Language code that uniquely identifies a locale. Valid examples would be 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'de-DE' etc. according to [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

selector.description: Act on the triggering text or matching target texts of its segment.

AutomationTargetSelector.description: Which texts the action changes. `TRIGGERING_TEXT`: the text that started the rule. `SEGMENT_TARGET_TEXTS`: the segment's texts in the target languages, optionally limited by `language_codes` and `conditions`; only a status rule that reacts to the source text can use it.

AutomationTrigger.description: What starts the rule. `KEY_CREATED`, `KEY_UPDATED` and `KEY_CREATED_OR_UPDATED`: a key is created, changed, or either; only `LABEL` rules can react to keys. `TEXT_CREATED`, `TEXT_UPDATED` and `TEXT_CREATED_OR_UPDATED`: a text is created, changed, or either.

AutomationType.description: The rule family. It decides the rule's action and how the family's matching rules run. `TEXT` replaces text (`REPLACE_TEXT`): every matching rule applies, in list order, so the replacements chain. `STATUS` sets a status (`SET_STATUS`): the first matching rule wins and the others are skipped. `LABEL` adds a label (`ADD_LABEL`): every matching rule applies. The families run in this order: text replacements first, then status changes, then labels.

stack_assignment.description: Optional complete stack assignment. Omission or null invites to the workspace only.

CreateKey.description: Request body to create a key in a file, with a new segment and its source text.

group_key.description: The group of the key, in formats with one group only (`key_type` REQUIRED_KEY_WITH_GROUP: PO, Qt TS, INI, Twine). Leaving it out or null creates the key without a group.

is_plural.description: Whether the segment has plural forms. The file's format must allow it. Defaults to false.

key.description: The full key, as the Key object shows it: nested keys join their parts with dots and put a part that is empty or contains a dot, a double quote or a backslash in double quotes, escaping quotes and backslashes with a backslash. The project's key normalization applies. At most 128 parts and 49,999 characters as stored, with the group.

label_ids.description: Labels of the workspace to add to the new segment. The stack's automations can add more.

source_variants.description: The source text, one variant per device and plural form, in this order. Leaving it out, null or `[]` creates the key with an empty source text. At most 1,048,576 characters in total.

items.description: The keys to create, in this order, each like the body of createKey. At most 1,048,576 characters of source text in total.

CreateLabel.description: Request body to create a label.

ai_context.example: Short, catchy texts for marketing campaigns

color.description: Hex color code of the new label (e.g., #FF5733). Without it, the label gets one of the default label colors.

name.description: Display name of the new label. Must be unique within the workspace (case-insensitive).

CreateLina.description: Request body to create a LINA whose engines you choose.

color.description: Color of the LINA's icon, as a hexadecimal RGB value. Defaults to `#C084FC`.

context.description: Which context the LINA sends along with each text it translates. A source left out is enabled when the engine supports it.

glossary_id.description: Glossary of the workspace the LINA uses for translation and for the terminology check. Left out or null: none.

is_tm_match_enabled.description: Whether the LINA reuses a translation-memory match with exactly the same source text instead of translating it. Defaults to `false`.

language_engine_overrides.description: Engines the LINA uses for single target languages instead of `linguistic_engine_id`, one per language. Defaults to none.

linguistic_engine_id.description: Engine the LINA translates with; it must be enabled in the workspace (GET /v2/linguistic-engines lists them).

name.description: Name of the LINA; it must be unique in the workspace, ignoring case.

restricted_stack_ids.description: Stacks of the workspace the LINA may work in; an empty list allows none. Left out or null: every stack.

style_guide_id.description: Style guide of the workspace the LINA follows when translating and for the style checks. Left out or null: none.

CreateLinaContext.description: Request body to choose the context a LINA sends along with each text. A source left out is enabled when the engine supports it.

is_glossary_enabled.description: Send the terms of the LINA's glossary.

is_labels_enabled.description: Send the labels of the segment.

is_segments_enabled.description: Send the description of the segment.

is_style_guide_enabled.description: Send the rules of the LINA's style guide.

is_translation_memory_enabled.description: Send similar translations from the translation memory.

CreateLinaExecution.description: Request body to pre-translate segments of a branch with the stack's LINA.

only_empty.description: Translate only texts without a translation; `false` also translates texts that already have one.

segment_ids.description: Segments of the branch to translate. Left out, every segment of the branch is translated.

target_language_codes.description: Target languages of the branch to translate into; each gets its own run.

items.description: Language code that uniquely identifies a locale. Valid examples would be 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'de-DE' etc. according to [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

name.description: The name of the project, 2 to 255 characters.

source_language_code.description: The source language code for the project.

An occupied private stack cannot accept another project. Existing stack configuration and access are retained; missing target languages are added stack-wide.

target_language_codes.description: Language codes of the project's target languages, at most 1000.

type.description: The project's file format; it decides which files the project accepts and can't be changed later.

language_code_separator.description: How the language is joined to the file name: `_`, `-` or `.`; Android XML also accepts `-r`.

path.description: Relative resource path template, preserved exactly. Include %{locale}; a mixed locale/file basename also needs %{language_code_separator}. Parent folders are created automatically.

forms.description: The term's forms. A language has at most one preferred form; an untranslatable term's forms have no language.

type.description: Whether the term is translated.

case_sensitivity.description: How the form is matched with regard to case. Defaults to SENSITIVE, as in the app.

inherited_by.description: Languages of the glossary without a form of their own that use this form, e.g. `de-AT` and `de-CH` for a `de` form. Only for the preferred form of a translatable term.

part_of_speech.description: Part of speech of the form.

usage_status.description: How the form should be used. Defaults to PREFERRED.

ImportGitSource.description: Repository head observed before this pull listed its files. Files are fetched through a mutable branch, so this is not an exact content-snapshot guarantee or a success flag. Imports without a complete retained observation, including ordinary uploads and historical jobs, have null git_source. Processing, partial and failed imports can retain an observation; inspect status and entries. A retry can replace the observation after another head read, or retain a previous observation if it fails earlier. Separate jobs retain independent observations. Reads never contact the provider or infer metadata from the current branch binding.

  - INCOMPLETE_TRANSLATION: LINA could not translate some of the selected texts.
  - INTERRUPTED: the run was interrupted and not repeated, because the engine may already have been called.
  - SELECTION_CHANGED: the selected segments left the branch, or the project moved to another stack; select the segments again.
  - EXECUTION_FAILED: an unexpected error stopped the run.

LinaExecutionStatus.description:
Where a LINA run stands. QUEUED and PROCESSING are pending; the others are final.
  - SUCCEEDED: every selected text was translated.
  - PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED: part of the selection was translated; `failure` says why the rest wasn't.
  - FAILED: nothing was translated, or the run stopped on an error; `failure` says why.
  - CANCELLED: the queued run was cancelled because its selection changed; `failure` says so.
  - SKIPPED: there was nothing to translate.

  - CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED: the workspace has no AI credits left.
  - CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED: the LINA or its engine has to be set up first.
  - PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED: the engine's provider needs action on your account, e.g. a key or billing.
  - PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: the engine's provider is unavailable for now; try again later.
  - LANGUAGE_PAIR_UNSUPPORTED: the engine doesn't translate between these languages.

content_version.description:
Version of this resource's exported content. A file's number moves whenever any of its languages moves and when a language is
added to or removed from it; a folder's number combines the numbers of the files below it and moves whenever any of them does. It increases whenever anything changes that could alter an export of the file (its segments, their texts and
statuses, keys, order, the file itself, the languages, the export settings, the branch). Compare it with the content_version of
your last export entry for the same file, language and export settings, and export again only when it moved. It tracks the
translatable data: a LingoHub release can still change how a format is rendered, and ARB embeds a generation timestamp -
re-export after a release when byte identity matters. Null for a file
without languages.

  - LTR: left-to-right (e.g. English, German)
  - RTL: right-to-left (e.g. Arabic, Hebrew)

TextStage.description:
The high-level workflow stage that groups one or more `TextStatus` values:
  - `NOT_READY` — blocked segments
  - `NEEDS_EDIT` — new, draft, stale or rejected segments
  - `NEEDS_REVIEW` — AI-translated, translated, QA-passed or QA-flagged segments
  - `DONE` — approved or not-translatable segments

TextStatus.description: The workflow status of texts in a given language. Each status belongs to exactly one `TextStage` (see the `stage` grouping in the status counts).

TextUpdateMode.description: When an import may change an existing text: `ALWAYS` overwrites it, `ONLY_EMPTY` only fills it when it's empty, `NEVER` keeps it.

TextVariant.description: One variant of a text: its content for a device and a plural form.

content.description: The text, with its placeholders and markup.

plural_form.description: Plural form of the variant; a segment without plural forms has OTHER only.

TransferContentIntegration.description: Request body to pull or push resources through the existing content integration.

language_codes.description: Language selection from the current default branch. Null or an empty list uses all eligible languages according to the provider workflow. Duplicate codes are rejected.

resource_ids.description: Resource selection in the project's current default branch. Null or an empty list selects all eligible resources, preserving the provider workflow. Duplicate identities are rejected.

items.description: Public id that is created from the type prefix of the corresponding resource and its UUID. I.e : For a resource container, a valid value would be : rc_0197c8f2-5a6b-7cde-8f12-3456789abcde

TransitionSegment.description: Request body to change the status of the segment's text in one language.

action.description: APPROVE approves the text and dismisses its quality findings, REOPEN reopens it, MARK_TRANSLATED marks a translation as translated, REJECT rejects a translation. The source text takes only APPROVE and REOPEN.

language_code.description: Language of the text, one of the stack's languages.

TransitionSegmentsBulk.description: Request body to change the status of up to 150 texts of a branch.

items.description: The status changes, each text once.

TranslateLina.description: Request body to translate plain texts with a LINA, outside any project. At most 16,384 characters in total.

source_language_code.description: Language of the texts; a supported locale.

target_language_code.description: Language to translate into; a supported locale other than the source.

texts.description: One to ten plain texts; `results[i]` of the response belongs to `texts[i]`. Whitespace is kept, and no file format or placeholders are assumed. The same text may be listed more than once.

UpdateBranch.description: Request body to partially update a branch (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; an omitted `name` is left unchanged. `name` cannot be null.

name.description: Display name of the branch; unique in the project.

UpdateContentIntegration.description: Request body to change which content a project syncs with its content platform (JSON merge-patch).

path_filters.description: The content the project syncs, replaced as a whole; empty for none. A change starts a sync of the default branch.

UpdateContextImage.description: Request body to partially update a context image (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields are left unchanged and an explicit `description: null` clears the description. `name` cannot be null.

description.description: Description of what the image shows. An explicit null clears it.
description.example: Screenshot of the checkout screen showing the payment options.

name.description: Display name of the context image. It can't be empty.

UpdateCsvFileFormat.description: Changes how CSV files are read and written, field by field.

description_header.description: The header of the column with the descriptions. Null: imports take the column headed Description or Comment, and exports leave the header empty.

is_import_detection_enabled.description: Let imports update detected CSV settings.

is_status_exported.description: Include status information in CSV output.

key_header.description: The header of the column with the keys. Null: imports take the column headed Title, Key or Id, and exports leave the header empty.

quote.description: The character that encloses a value.

UpdateEscapeFileFormat.description: Changes how special characters are written.

UpdateGeneralFileFormat.description: Changes the options every file format uses, field by field.

charset.description: The character encoding of exported files.

comment_languages.description: Which exported files carry comments; null: no file does.

file_name_languages.description: Which exported files carry their language code in the file name or path.

indentation.description: Spaces per indentation level, 0 to 100; null uses 2.

auto_push_default_branch_type.description: How the default branch is pushed when its translations are complete.

auto_push_other_branches_type.description: How other branches are pushed when their translations are complete.

commit_description.description: Commit description template; may be empty.

pull_request_branch.description: Template of the branch a pull request comes from.

pull_request_description.description: Pull request description template; may be empty.

push_type.description: Whether a push commits to the branch or opens a pull request.

UpdateGitSelection.description: Which files and branches LingoHub syncs (JSON merge-patch; lists are replaced as a whole). Branch filters exist only while branching: turning branching off drops them.

branch_filters.description: The remote branches LingoHub keeps a branch for; only while branching. New branch filters add or remove the branches they select.

is_branching.description: Whether LingoHub keeps a branch for every remote branch `branch_filters` select. Turning it off deletes every branch except the default one.

path_filters.description: The files LingoHub syncs; empty for none. New path filters start an import on every branch.

UpdateGitSync.description: When LingoHub pulls and pushes by itself (JSON merge-patch). A schedule exists only for a `PERIODIC` mode: entering `PERIODIC` needs one, leaving it drops it.

export_schedule.description: When LingoHub pushes; required for `PERIODIC`, null otherwise.

import_schedule.description: When LingoHub pulls; required for `PERIODIC`, null otherwise.

UpdateGlossary.description: Request body to change a glossary with JSON merge-patch: a field left out keeps its value, and `language_codes` replaces the whole list. Neither field can be null.

language_codes.description: Languages the glossary covers, each once, replacing the current list; every one a supported locale (GET /v2/locales lists them).

name.description: Name of the glossary.

UpdateI18nextFileFormat.description: Changes how i18next JSON files are read and written, field by field.

version.description: The i18next JSON version of the files.

UpdateIntegrationAuthentication.description: Request body to rename a stored authentication. Omitted name leaves it unchanged; null is not accepted. Credentials and provider lifecycle are unchanged.

name.description: Authentication display name.

UpdateJsonFileFormat.description: Changes how JSON files are laid out, field by field.

UpdateKey.description: Request body to rename a key with JSON merge-patch.

group_key.description: The group, in formats with one group only (`key_type` REQUIRED_KEY_WITH_GROUP: PO, Qt TS, INI, Twine). Leaving it out keeps the group; null removes it.

key.description: The full key, as the Key object shows it and createKey takes it. At most 128 parts and 49,999 characters as stored, with the group; a longer existing key can be sent back unchanged. Leaving it out keeps the key; null isn't accepted.

UpdateLabel.description: Request body to partially update a label (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `ai_context` may be set to null to clear it; `name` and `color` cannot be null.

ai_context.description: Tells LINA what segments with this label are about. A LINA with an AI engine reads it when its `context.is_labels_enabled` is on; LingoHub-managed LINAs always do. Null clears it.
ai_context.example: Short, catchy texts for marketing campaigns

color.description: Hex color code of the label (e.g., #FF5733).

name.description: Display name of the label. Must be unique within the workspace (case-insensitive).

UpdateLina.description: Request body to change a LINA with JSON merge-patch: a field left out keeps its value, `null` clears a nullable field and lists replace the whole list.

color.description: Color of the LINA's icon, as a hexadecimal RGB value.

context.description: Which context the LINA sends along with each text; a source left out keeps its value.

description.description: Description of the LINA; null clears it.

glossary_id.description: Glossary of the workspace the LINA uses for translation and for the terminology check; null: none.

is_tm_match_enabled.description: Whether the LINA reuses a translation-memory match with exactly the same source text instead of translating it.

language_engine_overrides.description: Engines the LINA uses for single target languages, replacing the current list; one per language. Can't be set for a LingoHub-managed LINA.

linguistic_engine_id.description: Engine the LINA translates with; it must be enabled in the workspace. Can't be changed for a LingoHub-managed LINA.

name.description: Name of the LINA; it must stay unique in the workspace, ignoring case.

restricted_stack_ids.description: Stacks of the workspace the LINA may work in, replacing the current list; an empty list allows none. null: every stack.

style_guide_id.description: Style guide of the workspace the LINA follows when translating and for the style checks; null: none.

UpdateLinaContext.description: Request body to change the context a LINA sends along with each text.

is_glossary_enabled.description: Send the terms of the LINA's glossary.

is_labels_enabled.description: Send the labels of the segment.

is_segments_enabled.description: Send the description of the segment.

is_style_guide_enabled.description: Send the rules of the LINA's style guide.

is_translation_memory_enabled.description: Send similar translations from the translation memory.

UpdateLinaQualityRuleSettings.description: Request body to change one quality-check rule; a field left out keeps its value.

severity.description: How severe the rule's findings are.

UpdateLinaQualityRules.description: Request body to change quality-check rules; a rule left out keeps its settings.

length_constraints.description: Changes to the length constraints rule.

locale_formatting.description: Changes to the locale formatting rule.

quotes_and_delimiters.description: Changes to the quotes and delimiters rule.

UpdateLinaQualitySettings.description: Request body to change a LINA's quality-check settings with JSON merge-patch: a rule or field left out keeps its value, and `translatable_html_attributes` replaces the whole list.

is_html_attribute_check_enabled.description: Whether the markup checks inspect the values of HTML attributes.

rules.description: Rules to change; a rule left out keeps its settings.

translatable_html_attributes.description: Names of the HTML attributes whose values are translated, replacing the current list; each name once.

UpdateMember.description: Request body to update a non-owner workspace member's role while preserving explicit stack assignments.

workspace_role_id.description: Existing non-owner workspace role. Omission preserves the current role; null is not allowed.

UpdateProject.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub project (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `ai_context` and `website` may be set to null to clear them; `name` and `color` cannot be null.

ai_context.description: Context that tells LINA what the project is about; LINA gets it together with the stack's context. `null` removes it.
ai_context.example: Updated project context.

color.description: Hex color code of the project icon.

name.description: The name of the project, 2 to 255 characters.

website.description: A website for the project, at most 256 characters. `null` removes it.

html_encoding.description: How exports write HTML in the formats that support it.

source_empty_content_handling.description: What an export does with an empty source text.

source_statuses.description: The statuses a source text needs to be exported.

target_empty_content_handling.description: What an export does with an empty target text.

target_statuses.description: The statuses a target text needs to be exported.

UpdateProjectFormatSettings.description: The options of the project's file format, in sections. Which sections a project needs depends on its type: `general` for every file-based type except DOCUMENT; `csv` for STANDARD_CSV, SINGLE_LANGUAGE_CSV and KEY_VALUE_CSV; `escape` for STANDARD_PROPERTIES and STANDARD_INI; `json` for STANDARD_ARB, STANDARD_JSON, ANGULAR_TRANSLATE_JSON, CHROME_I18N_JSON, GO_I18N_JSON, I18NEXT_JSON, REACT_INTL_JSON and VUE_I18N_JSON; `i18next_json` for I18NEXT_JSON; `xliff` for STANDARD_XLIFF; `properties` for STANDARD_PROPERTIES. A section the type doesn't need has no effect.

csv.description: CSV options; changed field by field, null removes them.

escape.description: Escaping options; changed field by field, null removes them.

general.description: Options every file format uses; changed field by field.

i18next_json.description: i18next options; changed field by field, null removes them.

json.description: JSON options; changed field by field, null removes them.

properties.description: Properties options; changed field by field, null removes them.

xliff.description: XLIFF options; changed field by field, null removes them.

UpdateProjectGitIntegration.description: Request body to change a project's git integration (JSON merge-patch): send only what changes. A new connection, repository or `git_branch` is checked with the git host, as when connecting the project.

git_branch.description: The remote branch the project's default branch syncs with; the default branch is renamed after it.

name.description: The repository's name.

namespace.description: The repository's namespace, as the repository lookups name it; empty for CodeCommit.

selection.description: Which files and branches LingoHub syncs.

sync.description: When LingoHub pulls and pushes by itself.

UpdateProjectHubSpotIntegration.description: Request body to change which HubSpot content a project syncs (JSON merge-patch; lists are replaced as a whole).

enabled_content_types.description: The kinds of HubSpot content the project syncs. Saved and applied from the next sync.

path_filters.description: The content the project syncs, matched against content paths; empty for none. A change starts a sync of the default branch.

is_source_creation_enabled.description: Whether imports may create source text entries.

is_source_deactivation_enabled.description: Whether imports may deactivate source entries missing from the input.

is_source_metadata_update_enabled.description: Whether imports may update source metadata.

is_target_creation_enabled.description: Whether imports may create target text entries.

is_target_deactivation_enabled.description: Whether imports may deactivate target entries missing from the input.

is_target_metadata_update_enabled.description: Whether imports may update target metadata.

source_text_update_mode.description: When imports may update an existing source text.

target_text_update_mode.description: When imports may update an existing target text.

UpdateProjectIntegrationSettings.description: Changes what a sync of the project's integration deletes; applies from the next sync.

is_removed_language_deletion_enabled.description: Whether a sync deletes languages the integration no longer reports. The source language is never deleted. Only Contentful, HubSpot, Storyblok, Stripo and Zendesk integrations read this setting; Git and Crisp integrations never delete languages. Enabled by default for Contentful, Zendesk and Storyblok integrations.

is_removed_resource_deletion_enabled.description: Whether a Git repository pull deletes files the repository no longer contains. Only Git integrations read this setting; the other integrations always delete resources a sync no longer reports. Enabled by default for Git integrations.

normalization_strategy.description: How keys are normalised when they are imported, created or renamed. Existing keys aren't renamed.

UpdateProjectLanguage.description: Request body to change a project language (JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields stay unchanged; `file_slug: null` removes the slug. The fallback language and LINA role are set on the stack language with updateStackLanguage.

file_slug.description: The language's name in this project's file names, used instead of the language code; null uses the language code.

UpdateProjectPlaceholderSettings.description: Changes which placeholders are recognised. `default_definitions` and `is_default` are read-only.

definitions.description: The placeholder kinds recognised in texts; the first that matches wins. Empty: none. Send `default_definitions` to go back to the defaults.

UpdateProjectSettings.description: Request body to change a project's settings (JSON merge-patch): send only the sections and fields that change, also inside the sections of `format`. Lists are replaced as a whole; null removes a `format` section.

format.description: File-format options. Null removes them, which only documents and integration projects allow.

integrations.description: Integration settings; only for a project that has an integration.

UpdatePropertiesFileFormat.description: Changes how properties files name plural forms.

plural_separator.description: The text between a key and its plural form, such as `_` in `apples_one`.

UpdateResource.description: Request body to partially update a resource (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields are left unchanged. Renaming the `path` also moves the resource and its sub-resources within the branch.

language_code_separator.description: How the language is joined to the file name: `_`, `-` or `.`; Android XML also accepts `-r`.

path.description: New full path of the resource within the branch: relative, segments separated by `/`, the last one naming the resource. No empty or `..` segment, no segment longer than 255 characters. A file path must retain `%{locale}` somewhere in the path. When its basename combines `%{locale}` with other text, use `%{language_code_separator}` as the separator, for example `messages%{language_code_separator}%{locale}.json`. Keep an extension allowed by the resource's format. A folder path does not need a locale placeholder.

UpdateSegment.description: Request body to change a segment and its texts with JSON merge-patch. Changes apply to every key of the segment.

description.description: Note for translators. A LINA with an AI engine reads it too when its `context.is_segments_enabled` is on; LingoHub-managed LINAs always do. Null clears it.

is_not_translatable.description: Whether the segment is excluded from translation.

is_plural.description: Whether the segment has plural forms. The formats of all its files must allow it. Becoming singular keeps the OTHER form and removes the other plural forms in all languages.

label_ids.description: Replaces the segment's labels with these labels of the workspace; `[]` removes them all. At most 150.

texts.description: The texts to change, by language code; languages left out keep their text. `variants` replaces a language's text, and `[]` clears it.

UpdateSegmentText.description: Request body part that replaces the text of a segment in one language.

is_minor_update.description: Whether the change is minor, such as a typo fix: the status automations for minor edits apply, so the translations of a changed source text can stay as they are. Defaults to false.

variants.description: The new text, one variant per device and plural form, in this order. It replaces the language's text; `[]` clears it. At most 1,000 variants.

UpdateSegmentsBulk.description: Request body to change up to 150 segments of a branch.

items.description: The segments to change, each once. At most 1,048,576 characters of text in total.

UpdateStack.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub stack (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged; `name` and `color` cannot be null, a null `ai_context` or `lina_id` removes it.

ai_context.description: Context that tells LINA what the stack is about, given with the project's own.
ai_context.example: Mobile apps for retail banking.

color.description: Hex color code of the stack icon.

lina_id.description: LINA of the workspace to assign to the stack; null removes the assignment. The stack languages keep their `lina_role`. Setting or removing it requires stack-level languages management permission, besides the settings management permission of the operation.

name.description: Display name of the stack.

UpdateStackLanguage.description: Request body to change a stack language (JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields stay unchanged; `lina_role` can't be null, `fallback_language_code: null` removes the fallback.

fallback_language_code.description: The language used when a translation in this language is missing: another language of the stack, without loops. It applies to every project of the stack; `null` removes it.

lina_role.description: What the stack's LINA does in this language. Has no effect while the stack has no LINA.

UpdateStackMember.description: Request body to merge an existing stack assignment's role and explicit language permissions.

language_permissions.description: Map entries are merged, not replaced. Omission or an empty map preserves explicit rows; a null value removes that locale's explicit row. The map itself cannot be null. This describes stored configuration, not effective access.

stack_role_id.description: Existing non-owner stack role. Omission preserves it; null is invalid.

UpdateStyleGuide.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub style guide (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `name` and `rules` cannot be null; `ai_context` and `audience_description` may be set to null to clear them, and each rule inside `rules` may be set to null to reset it to `NOT_SPECIFIED`.

ai_context.description: Additional context provided to the AI to guide translation style and tone.
ai_context.example: Translate in a friendly and approachable tone suitable for a SaaS product.

audience_description.description: Description of the target audience for this style guide.
audience_description.example: Software developers and technical users familiar with localization workflows.

name.description: Display name of the style guide.

rules.description: Style rules to change (JSON merge-patch): omitted rules are left unchanged, a rule set to null is reset to NOT_SPECIFIED.

UpdateStyleGuideRules.description: Style rules to change (JSON merge-patch): omitted rules are left unchanged, a rule set to null is reset to NOT_SPECIFIED.

age_group.description: Target age group for translation style and vocabulary choice.

audience.description: Target audience for translation style and vocabulary choice.

domain.description: Content domain to guide context-specific AI behavior.

formality.description: Desired level of formality for translated text.

grammatical_person.description: Grammatical person to use for translated text.

language_complexity.description: Desired level of language complexity for generated text.

literal_translation.description: Specifies how literally the source text should be translated.

vocabulary_type.description: Type of vocabulary to guide AI word choice.

voice.description: Preferred grammatical voice for translated text.

UpdateTerm.description: Request body to partially update a term (JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. The forms have their own endpoints.

ai_context.description: Context for AI translation. Null clears it.
ai_context.example: Final step of the purchase flow.

enforcement_status.description: How strictly the term is applied.

UpdateTermForm.description: Request body to change a term form with JSON merge-patch: a field left out keeps its value, null clears a nullable field. The language of a form cannot change: add a form in the other language and delete this one instead.

case_sensitivity.description: How the form is matched with regard to case.

form_type.description: Lexical type of the form. Null clears it.

grammatical_gender.description: Grammatical gender of the form. Null clears it.

grammatical_number.description: Grammatical number of the form. Null clears it.

inherited_by.description: Languages of the glossary without a form of their own that use this form. Replaces the current list; only for the preferred form of a translatable term. A language removed from the list keeps a copy of the form.

match_expression.description: The regular expression a `CUSTOM` matching uses. Null clears it.

matching.description: How the form is matched against text; `AUTOMATIC` only for languages that support it, also the inheriting ones.

part_of_speech.description: Part of speech of the form. Null clears it.

usage_status.description: How the form should be used.

UpdateWebhookEndpoint.description: Request body to change a webhook endpoint. Omitted fields stay unchanged; null clears description or scope. To move the endpoint between a stack and a project, send the new id and null for the old one. event_types replaces the whole list.

description.description: Description of the endpoint; null clears it.

event_types.description: Events to receive, replacing the whole list, as listed by listWebhookEventTypes, or ["*"] for all events.

project_id.description: Limits deliveries to the events of this project; null clears it. At most one of stack_id and project_id.

stack_id.description: Limits deliveries to the events of this stack and its projects; null clears it. At most one of stack_id and project_id.

url.description: Public HTTPS address deliveries are sent to; checked as on create.

UpdateWorkspaceApiKey.description: Request body to partially update active workspace-managed key metadata without changing its permissions or ownership.

expiration_date.description: Last valid day, inclusive, in UTC. Null means no configured expiration.

name.description: Display name, unique among workspace-managed keys.

UpdateXliffFileFormat.description: Changes how XLIFF files identify keys and languages, field by field.

UsageStatus.description:
How a term form should be used:
  - PREFERRED: the recommended form. A language of a term has at most one preferred form.
  - ADMITTED: an accepted alternative form.
  - NOT_RECOMMENDED: a discouraged or deprecated form.

VariantPluralForm.description: Plural form of a text variant.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event sent to one endpoint: its status, attempts, next retry, the last response, and the request that is sent.

created_at.description: When the delivery was queued.

delivered_at.description: When the endpoint accepted the delivery; null until it has.

event_id.description: The event that is sent; also the webhook-id header of the request.

event_type.description: Public event name; null only for an event type this LingoHub version doesn't know yet.

id.description: Unique identifier of the webhook delivery.

last_duration_ms.description: How long the last attempt took, in milliseconds.

last_error.description: Short fixed text explaining why the last attempt failed, such as `non-2xx response: 503` or `The endpoint did not respond in time.`; null when no attempt failed.

last_response_body.description: Body of the endpoint's answer to the last failed attempt, cut at 8192 bytes; null when there was none.

last_response_status.description: HTTP status the endpoint answered the last attempt with; null without a response.

max_attempts.description: Attempts the delivery gets before it is given up.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due; null when none is scheduled.

request.description: The request that is sent, rebuilt on each read from the event and the endpoint's current URL; the signature headers are not shown.

status.description: QUEUED waits for the first attempt or the next retry; PROCESSING is being sent; SUCCEEDED was accepted by the endpoint; FAILED was given up: `is_exhausted` true means all attempts were used, false that it stopped for another reason, e.g. a disabled endpoint.

updated_at.description: When the delivery last changed.

webhook_endpoint_id.description: The endpoint the delivery is sent to.

WebhookDeliveryCollection.description: A cursor-paginated collection of webhook delivery resources.

data.description: The list of items in this page.

has_more.description: True if more items exist after this page. Iterate by repeating the request with the cursor query parameter set to next_cursor until has_more is false.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token pointing past the last item of this page. Null on the last page. Pass it unchanged via the cursor query parameter to request the next page.

WebhookDeliveryFilter.description: The filter of a list: which items to return and in which order.

sort.description: Fields to sort by, in order: `+` ascending, `-` descending.

WebhookDeliveryFilterClause.description: A nested `_and`/`_or`, or one field with one operator.

webhook_delivery[attempt_count].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

_within.description: The lower and the upper bound.

webhook_delivery[created_at].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

_within.description: The lower and the upper bound.

webhook_delivery[event_id].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

webhook_delivery[id].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

webhook_delivery[status].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

webhook_delivery[updated_at].description: Exactly one operator of the field.

_within.description: The lower and the upper bound.

WebhookDeliveryFilterGroup.description: Exactly one of `_and` and `_or`, with the clauses it combines.

WebhookDeliveryJob.description: A webhook delivery scheduled for asynchronous processing.

data.description: The queued delivery. Poll the Location while QUEUED or PROCESSING; SUCCEEDED and FAILED are terminal.

WebhookEndpoint.description: An address LingoHub sends the subscribed events of one stack, one project or the whole workspace to. The signing secret is never included.

api_version.description: Payload format the endpoint was created with.

consecutive_failures.description: Failed deliveries in a row since the last success; at 15 the endpoint is switched off.

created_at.description: When the endpoint was created.

description.description: Description of the endpoint; null when it has none.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was switched off; null while it is enabled.

event_types.description: Subscribed events, as listed by listWebhookEventTypes; ["*"] subscribes to all events, including those added later.

id.description: Unique identifier of the webhook endpoint.

last_failure_at.description: When a delivery attempt last failed; null if none has yet.

last_success_at.description: When a delivery last succeeded; null if none has yet.

project_id.description: Project whose events the endpoint receives. At most one of stack_id and project_id is set; neither means the whole workspace.

stack_id.description: Stack whose events the endpoint receives, its projects included. At most one of stack_id and project_id is set; neither means the whole workspace.

status.description: ENABLED receives deliveries. DISABLED was switched off by hand. AUTO_DISABLED was switched off by LingoHub after 15 failed deliveries in a row. Both stay off until the endpoint is enabled.

updated_at.description: When the endpoint was last changed.

url.description: Public HTTPS address deliveries are sent to.

WebhookEndpointCollection.description: A cursor-paginated collection of webhook endpoint resources.

data.description: The list of items in this page.

has_more.description: True if more items exist after this page. Iterate by repeating the request with the cursor query parameter set to next_cursor until has_more is false.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token pointing past the last item of this page. Null on the last page. Pass it unchanged via the cursor query parameter to request the next page.

WebhookEndpointFilter.description: The filter of a list: which items to return and in which order.

info.description:
> **Beta:** API V2 is in beta. Endpoints, request and response fields, and behavior can still change. Use the LingoHub CLI (`lingohub`) where possible: it is updated together with the API. If you call the HTTP API directly, be prepared to update your integration when V2 changes.

The LingoHub V2 API provides programmatic access to your localization workflow. Use it to manage workspaces, projects, resources, translations, and more.

## Authentication

All requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. API keys can be created in the LingoHub workspace settings and use the `lh-api_` prefix.

```
Authorization: Bearer lh-api_your_api_key_here
```

## Pagination

List endpoints use cursor pagination via the `cursor` and `limit` query parameters (`limit` defaults to 20, maximum 100). Each response contains the returned items in `data`, a `has_more` flag, and an opaque `next_cursor` token that is null on the last page. To iterate a collection, repeat the request with `cursor` set to the previous response's `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false. Keep all other query parameters identical while iterating — a cursor is bound to the collection (parent resource), the filters, and the sort order it was created under and is rejected with an `invalid_cursor` error otherwise. Total counts are intentionally not provided; items created or deleted before the cursor position are not revisited during an iteration.

## Filtering

Lists take a `filter` query parameter: URL-encoded JSON that selects the items to return (`where`) and orders them (`sort`). `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is a nested `_and`/`_or`, or a field with exactly one operator. Fields are named `<object_type>[<field>]` after the list's items, e.g. `project[name]`, and compare the values the responses show. Each list documents its fields, their operators and values, and which of them sort, in its `filter` parameter and its schema (`ProjectFilter`, ...). A field, operator or value a list does not support answers `400 invalid_filter`, with an error pointing into the filter and naming what is supported there.

### Operators

A clause compares one field with one operator: `{ "<field>": { "<operator>": <value> } }`.

| Operator | Matches items whose field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `_eq`, `_ne` | equals / does not equal the value | one value |
| `_in`, `_nin` | is one of / none of the values | non-empty array |
| `_lt`, `_lte`, `_gt`, `_gte` | is less than / at most / greater than / at least the value | number or timestamp |
| `_within` | lies between the two bounds, both included | `[lower, upper]` |
| `_contains`, `_ncontains` | contains / does not contain the text, case-sensitive | text |
| `_icontains`, `_nicontains` | contains / does not contain the text, ignoring case | text |
| `_starts`, `_ends` | starts / ends with the text, case-sensitive | text |
| `_like`, `_nlike` | matches / does not match a pattern, case-sensitive: `%` stands for any text, `_` for one character | text |
| `_ilike`, `_nilike` | like `_like` and `_nlike`, ignoring case | text |
| `_blank`, `_nblank` | has no text (missing or empty) / has text | `true` |
| `_null`, `_nnull` | has no value / has a value | `true` |
| `_true`, `_false` | is true / is false | `true` |

Which operators a field offers depends on its type:

| Field type | Operators |
|---|---|
| text | `_eq` `_ne` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_blank` `_nblank` |
| id, enum | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` |
| integer | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` `_lt` `_lte` `_gt` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` |
| timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_lte` `_gt` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` |
| boolean | `_true` `_false` |

Values have the form the responses show: public ids (`stack_0197c8f2-…`), enum values (`STANDARD_JSON`), and timestamps in RFC 3339 UTC (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Each list operation shows its own fields in a table under its `filter` parameter in the API reference: the field name, its type, the operators it offers and whether it can sort.

More clauses:

```json
{ "project[type]": { "_in": ["STANDARD_JSON", "I18NEXT_JSON"] } }
{ "import[created_at]": { "_within": ["2026-11-01T00:00:00Z", "2026-11-30T23:59:59Z"] } }
{ "invitation[accepted_at]": { "_null": true } }
{ "branch[is_default]": { "_false": true } }
{ "key[key]": { "_like": "checkout.%" } }
```

### Example

```json
{
  "where": {
    "_and": [
      { "project[name]": { "_icontains": "app" } },
      {
        "_or": [
          { "project[type]": { "_eq": "STANDARD_JSON" } },
          { "project[created_at]": { "_gte": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" } }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "sort": ["-project[created_at]"]
}
```

An unknown value is answered with where it is and what the field accepts:

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "code": "invalid_filter",
  "errors": [
    {
      "parameter": "filter",
      "pointer": "#/where/_and/1/_or/0/project[type]/_eq",
      "code": "enum",
      "detail": "'JSON' is not a value of 'project[type]'. Values: ANDROID_XML, IOS_STRINGS, ..."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Rate limiting

Requests are rate limited per API key and per workspace (aggregate across all of its keys). Exceeding either limit returns `429 rate_limit_exceeded` with a `Retry-After` header stating the seconds to wait before retrying. Responses to authenticated requests additionally carry the structured `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `RateLimit-Policy` lists the applied policies with their request quota `q` per window of `w` seconds, and `RateLimit` reports the policy currently closest to rejection with the requests remaining right now (`r`) and the seconds until the full quota is available again (`t`). Use them to pace request rates proactively instead of backing off on 429 — but treat them as advisory: they are absent when the request fails authentication or the limiter state is momentarily unknown.

## Errors

All error responses follow the RFC 9457 Problem Details format with additional `code` and `request_id` fields for machine-readable error handling and support requests, and an additional `errors` field for handling multiple validation errors at once.

The field-level validation errors return a JSON pointer to the problem value, a detail description, and a machine-readable code. For more information, see RFC 9457 Section 3 §7.

Optional If-Match uses the validator of `getApiKey`; a stale one returns 412. Requires a personal API key.

post.description: Stores a connection to a git host or content platform from a token or keys you enter. Content-platform credentials are checked with the provider first; git tokens are stored as given and only fail when an integration uses them. GitHub is connected by installing the GitHub App (getGitHubInstallationLink). Requires workspace-level integration management permission.

parameters.description: Optional. A unique key of 1 to 255 characters, such as a UUID, for best-effort retry protection. A retry with the same key and request returns the stored success, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of running again; if none was stored, for example after a server error, it returns `409 idempotency_outcome_unknown`. Once the stored key expires (24 hours by default) or is lost, the request runs again. A different request with the same key fails with `422 idempotency_key_mismatch`, and a retry while the first still runs with `409 idempotency_key_in_use`. See [Safe retries](https://developers.lingohub.com/docs/api-v2-safe-retries#idempotency-keys-for-post-requests).
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: An unresolved request returns `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without Retry-After; inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation. A recent request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (`idempotency_key_in_use`); retry after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait for an in-progress keyed request; absent for other conflicts.

502.description: The content platform could not check the credentials (`upstream_error`). Nothing is stored; retry later.

delete.description: Deletes the connection, and with it the git or content integration of every project that uses it; the projects and their texts stay. The credentials aren't revoked at the provider: revoke the token or uninstall the GitHub App there yourself. Send the ETag from getIntegrationAuthentication as If-Match to make sure nobody changed it in between. Requires workspace-level integration management permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional. The quoted `ETag` from a `GET` of this resource; for an action, the `ETag` of the resource it acts on. The change is applied only if the resource still has that version; otherwise the request fails with `412 precondition_failed` and changes nothing. See [Conditional updates](https://developers.lingohub.com/docs/api-v2-safe-retries#conditional-updates-with-etags).
parameters.name: If-Match

post.description:
Uploads an image, at most 10 MB, that shows the UI text of one project language.

- Without `rendered_strings`, LingoHub reads the text in the image after the upload and links the segments it finds; with `auto_connect_suggestions: false` they stay suggestions to review in the app. Those links aren't in the response yet.
- With `rendered_strings`, as the iOS and Android SDKs send them, the image is linked right away to the segments whose keys or text match, and no text recognition runs. `[]` uploads the image without links.
- With `capture_key`, uploading the same screen again keeps the image's id: identical bytes change nothing (200 `UNCHANGED`); changed bytes replace the file and rebuild all its links, including ones added by hand (200 `REPLACED`). A new image answers 201 `CREATED`.

Every stored upload counts toward the workspace's monthly context image uploads. A segment keeps its three most recently linked images; linking a fourth detaches the oldest. Requires project-level context-image management permission.

post.description: Stops deliveries to the endpoint until it is enabled again. Events that happen while it is off are not sent, and deliveries still waiting for a retry fail; a request already on its way may still arrive. An auto-disabled endpoint becomes disabled and keeps its `disabled_at`. Does nothing if the endpoint is already disabled. Send the ETag from GET as If-Match to make sure nobody changed the endpoint in between. Requires workspace-level API access management permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional. A unique key of 1 to 255 characters, such as a UUID, for best-effort retry protection. A retry with the same key and request returns the stored success, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of running again; if none was stored, for example after a server error, it returns `409 idempotency_outcome_unknown`. Once the stored key expires (24 hours by default) or is lost, the request runs again. A different request with the same key fails with `422 idempotency_key_mismatch`, and a retry while the first still runs with `409 idempotency_key_in_use`. See [Safe retries](https://developers.lingohub.com/docs/api-v2-safe-retries#idempotency-keys-for-post-requests).
